extraction.notes: Research-log claims extracted from the available document content; numerical results remain UNVERIFIED and scoped to the stated fixtures.

claims.normalized_claim: The village-box cultivation document is a research note and scratch experiment log, not binding architecture or a skill.
claims.subject: village-box-cultivation

claims.normalized_claim: The reported experiments operate on scratch data and do not mutate shaded-engine runtime, analyze, classGrid or the spatial kernel.
claims.subject: village-box-cultivation

claims.normalized_claim: Most percentages through sections 1–4s come from one LOD0 source image and are not general operator-performance claims.
claims.subject: village-box-cultivation

claims.normalized_claim: The first cross-image VP result reported in section 4t reuses the LOD0 fit on structurally different LOD1 and separates 6 of 6 houses.
claims.subject: vanishing-point-fit

claims.normalized_claim: A holdout cross-validation reported in section 4g reduces threshold-selection circularity and yields 43.8% versus 38.6%.
claims.subject: segmentation

claims.normalized_claim: Fixed color values learned from VLG-02 fail to transfer to the second image in the section 4h test and yield no usable houses.
claims.subject: color-transfer

claims.normalized_claim: An image-local size-plus-geometry search on VLG-04 finds at least one structurally coherent roof-like region but not a complete reconstructed house.
claims.subject: geometry-search

claims.normalized_claim: The assumption that all six houses share one orientation is not proven from the 2D image alone.
claims.subject: orientation

claims.normalized_claim: The pooled orientation fit is reported as 8 to 45 times closer to the orthogonal ideal than individual-house fits, supporting shared orientation plus extraction noise without constituting strict proof.
claims.subject: orientation

claims.normalized_claim: The fake-LiDAR benchmark contains six houses, six faces per house, 225 points per face and 8100 points total.
claims.subject: fake-lidar

claims.normalized_claim: Geometry-only segmentation cleanly separates houses but leaks across faces and yields 6.3% point-weighted pure points.
claims.subject: geometry-segmentation

claims.normalized_claim: Adding RGB color to geometry raises point-weighted purity to 28.6%.
claims.subject: color-segmentation

claims.normalized_claim: Vanishing-point family snapping alone yields 1.6% pure points, while geometry plus color plus VP reaches 33.7%.
claims.subject: vp-segmentation

claims.normalized_claim: LBP texture signal is present between faces, but texture-only point-pair segmentation yields 0% pure points because pointwise LBP is the wrong granularity.
claims.subject: LBP

claims.normalized_claim: Geometry plus texture reaches 10.2% purity and geometry plus color plus texture reaches 35.4%.
claims.subject: LBP

claims.normalized_claim: A continuously updated region-average texture histogram reaches only 33.4% and is interpreted as suffering from region-growth contamination.
claims.subject: LBP

claims.normalized_claim: Freezing a small LBP anchor at size 5 with threshold 0.9 raises purity to 73.0%.
claims.subject: LBP

claims.normalized_claim: Increasing the frozen LBP anchor size from 5 to 20 to 50 reduces purity from 73.0% to 64.0% to 52.8%, supporting the contamination hypothesis.
claims.subject: LBP

claims.normalized_claim: A frozen VP anchor reaches 39.4% purity, while geometry plus frozen VP without color reaches 8.3%.
claims.subject: VP

claims.normalized_claim: Combining geometry, color, frozen VP and frozen LBP reaches 74.5% purity, only 1.5 percentage points above frozen LBP alone.
claims.subject: multichannel-fusion

claims.normalized_claim: The village site-plan reference images are maintainer-owned rather than third-party licensed assets.
claims.subject: site-plan-reference

claims.normalized_claim: The reference set contains three annotated isometric village site plans: two English variants and one German variant.
claims.subject: site-plan-reference

claims.normalized_claim: The English plans include building-position labels, feature labels and 0/5/10 metre scale bars.
claims.subject: site-plan-reference

claims.normalized_claim: The German plan includes BAUFLÄCHE A–F labels, infrastructure connection terminology, vegetation zones and a compass rose.
claims.subject: site-plan-reference

claims.normalized_claim: These plans are not valid blind reconstruction fixtures because building positions, scale and infrastructure information are already written into the images.
claims.subject: site-plan-reference

claims.normalized_claim: The plans are instead used as vocabulary, notation and scale references for spatial-construction and fixture-taxonomy documentation.
claims.subject: site-plan-reference
